segments.text: This episode takes place on Christmas Eve, and all three families are arguing about what Christmas is supposed to look like.
segments.tts_text: [a warm storyteller inviting the listener into the story] This episode takes place on Christmas Eve, and all three families are arguing about what Christmas is supposed to look like.

segments.text: At the Dunphy house, Claire finds a burn mark on the couch that looks like it came from a cigarette. None of the kids admits to smoking, so Phil makes a huge threat: if nobody tells the truth, Christmas is canceled.
segments.tts_text: [a natural conversational storyteller] At the Dunphy house, Claire finds a burn mark on the couch that looks like it came from a cigarette. None of the kids admits to smoking, so Phil makes a huge threat: if nobody tells the truth, Christmas is canceled.

segments.text: He and Claire take down the tree and decorations, expecting one of the kids to crack.
segments.tts_text: [a storyteller building gentle suspense] He and Claire take down the tree and decorations, expecting one of the kids to crack.

segments.text: The kids come up with their own plan. Luke is supposed to confess, and then Haley and Alex will both claim they did it too, hoping their parents will be so touched by their loyalty that they bring Christmas back. Luke does his part, but his sisters leave him hanging.

segments.text: He quickly takes the confession back, and Phil refuses to give in.

segments.text: Later, Alex comes downstairs and says she was the one smoking. She tells Phil he can punish her, but she doesn’t want everyone else to lose Christmas. The decorations go back up, and Alex gets grounded.

segments.text: Then sunlight shines through a glass ornament and starts burning the couch in exactly the same spot. Nobody smoked at all. Alex only took the blame to save Christmas, and Claire and Phil realize they punished the kids for something none of them did.

segments.text: Meanwhile, Jay is determined to have the same Christmas he had when Claire and Mitchell were young: new pajamas, a family picture on the stairs, presents in the morning, the whole routine.

segments.text: Gloria and Manny want some of their Colombian traditions too, like opening presents at midnight, setting off fireworks, and playing practical jokes. Jay keeps brushing them off because he wants Christmas done his way.

segments.text: After talking to Cameron, Jay realizes that having a new family means making new memories instead of trying to recreate the old ones. Gloria also explains to Manny why Jay cares so much about those traditions. In the end, both sides make an effort.

segments.text: Mitchell and Cameron take Lily to see Santa at the mall, but they complain that the Santa is too thin and end up getting him fired. Feeling guilty, they invite him home for dinner without admitting they caused the problem.

segments.text: Later, Cameron’s old caroling group shows up outside. They kicked him out, and Cameron is ready to turn the sprinklers on them. Scott, the former Santa, talks him into forgiving them. Cameron tries, but one of the singers insults him anyway. Scott immediately punches the guy.
